question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{3}-2.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{3}-2,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+2} & = \\ \frac{5-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}-2}{\sqrt{3}-2} & = \\ \frac{(5-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3}-2)}{(\sqrt{3}+2)(\sqrt{3}-2)} & = \\ \frac{5\sqrt{3}-10-(\sqrt{3})^{2}+2\sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}-(2)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{7\sqrt{3}-10-3}{3-4} & = \\ \frac{7\sqrt{3}-13}{-1} & = \\ 13-7\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
